q: 1. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: lime in excess, causes the cement to expand and disintegrate
silica in excess, causes the cement to set slowly
alumina in excess, reduces the strength of the cement
magnesium oxide in excess, remains in free state and makes the cement unsound
explain: All the listed effects of excess lime, silica, alumina, and magnesium oxide are correct statements regarding their influence on cement properties.

q: 2. During manufacturing process of portland cement, gypsum or plaster of paris is added
options: to increase the strength of cement
to modify the colour of cement
to adjust the setting time of cement
explain: Gypsum is added to cement clinker to control/retard the fast setting action of tricalcium aluminate (C3A), thereby adjusting the setting time of cement.

q: 3. Which of the following ingredient of cement when added in excess quantity, caused the cement to set slowly?
explain: Excess silica in cement makes the cement set slowly, as it increases the proportion of dicalcium silicate which hydrates and hardens slowly.

q: 4. The function of fine aggregate is:
options: to assist in producing workability and uniformity in the mixture
to assist the cement paste to hold the coarse aggregate particles in suspension
to promote plasticity in the mixture and prevent possible segregation of paste and coarse aggregate
explain: Fine aggregate serves multiple purposes in concrete — improving workability, uniformity, holding coarse particles in suspension, and preventing segregation — so all listed functions are correct.

q: 5. An aggregate generally should not preferred for use in concrete is one which has the following surface texture
explain: A glossy surface texture provides poor bond between the aggregate and cement paste, hence such aggregates are not preferred for concrete.

q: 6. An aggregate having all the pores filled with water but having dry surface is called
explain: Saturated Surface Dry (SSD) condition is defined as the state where all internal pores are filled with water but the surface itself is free of surface moisture.

q: 7. The maximum quantity of aggregate per 50 kg of cement should not exceed
explain: As per general guidelines, the total quantity of aggregate (fine plus coarse) used per 50kg bag of cement should not exceed about 450kg for good quality concrete.

q: 8. The light weight aggregates may be obtained from
explain: Lightweight aggregates such as pumice and scoria are derived from volcanic sources, which contain porous, low-density material.

q: 9. The void ratio of
options: single size coarse aggregate is roughly 0.45
explain: The void ratios given for single size coarse aggregate, graded coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate are all approximately correct as standard values.

q: 10. IS sieve No. 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
explain: IS sieves of 10 mm and 4.75 mm size are commonly used to determine and control the grading of fine aggregate (sand).

q: 11. The approx. ratio of direct tensile strength to flexural strength is
explain: The direct tensile strength of concrete is approximately half (0.5) of its flexural strength (modulus of rupture), since flexural tests measure extreme fiber stress differently from direct tension.

q: 12. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete on drying
explain: As moisture evaporates from ordinary cement concrete after casting, the paste loses volume and the concrete undergoes drying shrinkage.

q: 13. Inert material of a cement concrete mix, is
explain: Aggregate serves as the chemically inert filler material in a concrete mix, while cement and water are the active binding agents that react with each other.

q: 14. If aggregates completely pass through a sieve of size 75 mm and are retained on sieve of size 60 mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky is its minimum dimension is less than
explain: The mean dimension is the average of the two sieve sizes (75+60)/2 = 67.5mm; the flakiness criterion (least dimension < 3/5 of mean) gives 0.6 × 67.5 ≈ 40.5mm.

q: 15. The lime concrete has ......... strength as compared to cement concrete.
explain: Lime concrete develops significantly lower strength than cement concrete because lime is a weaker binder than Portland cement.

q: 16. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: Water cement paste hardens due to hydration
During hardening cement binds the aggregates together
Cement provides strength, durability and water tightness to the concrete
explain: All three statements correctly describe the role of cement: hardening via hydration, binding the aggregate particles, and imparting strength, durability, and impermeability to concrete.

q: 17. The diameter of the Vicat plunger is 10 mm and its length varies from
explain: As per IS specifications for the Vicat apparatus, the consistency plunger is 10 mm in diameter with a length in the range of 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 18. Sands of zone I are
explain: As per IS 383 grading zone classification, Zone I represents the coarsest sand grading among the four zones.

q: 19. Gypsum is added for
explain: Gypsum is interground with cement clinker specifically to retard the otherwise very rapid (flash) setting of tricalcium aluminate, thereby controlling and extending the setting time to a workable duration.

q: 20. Under normal conditions using an ordinary cement, the period of removal of the form work, is:
options: 15 days for bottom slabs 4.6 m and more
2 days for vertical sides of columns
explain: Standard formwork removal periods for ordinary cement concrete vary by member: about 2 days for columns, 7 days for beam soffits, and 15 days for larger slabs, so all these apply.

q: 21. Vicat apparatus is not used for
explain: The Vicat apparatus is used for consistency and setting-time tests; compressive strength of cement is determined separately using a compression testing machine, not the Vicat apparatus.

q: 22. Shrinkage in cement concrete is directly proportional to
explain: Shrinkage of concrete is primarily caused by the loss of water from the cement paste, so it is directly proportional to the water content present in the mix.

q: 23. Soundness test of cement by Le-Chatelier's apparatus gives unsoundness due to
explain: The Le Chatelier soundness test primarily detects unsoundness caused by excess free (uncombined) lime in the cement.

q: 24. Maximum permissible limit of magnesia content in OPC is
explain: As per IS 269 specifications, the maximum permissible magnesium oxide (magnesia) content in OPC is limited to 6%.

q: 25. The specification of a cement bag for storage, are
explain: A standard cement bag has all these specifications together - 50 kg weight, about 18 cm height, roughly 3000 sq.cm plan area, and about 35 litres volume.

q: 26. Ware house pack of cement means
options: pressure exertion of the bags of upper layers
pressure compaction of bags on lower layer
explain: 'Warehouse pack' refers to the compaction/packing effect experienced by the lower bags due to the pressure exerted by the weight of bags stacked above them.

q: 27. Light weight concrete is used for
explain: Due to its lower density and reduced structural strength, light weight concrete is mainly suitable for non-load bearing walls and partitions.

q: 28. Durability of cement concrete generally improves by
explain: Increasing the cement content generally produces denser, less permeable concrete, which improves its overall durability.

q: 29. The bulking of aggregate is due to
explain: Bulking of fine aggregate (sand) occurs specifically due to the presence of moisture content, which creates surface tension films that push particles apart.

q: 30. Early setting of cement can be attained by the addition of
explain: Calcium chloride is a well-known accelerating admixture that speeds up the setting and early hardening of cement, unlike gypsum which retards setting.

q: 31. In making pre cast structural units for partition and wall lining purposes, the concrete should be
explain: Light weight concrete, being easier to handle and providing better insulation, is preferred for precast partition and wall-lining units.

q: 32. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a
explain: The raw mix of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a rotary kiln, the standard equipment used in modern cement manufacture.

q: 33. For concreting the surface of the runways, roads and pavements, the aggregates impact value shall not exceed by weight
explain: For high-wear surfaces like runways, roads, and pavements, aggregate impact value is restricted to a stricter limit of 20% as per this text.

q: 34. If the effective plan area of a ware house is 54 m2 and the maximum height of pile permitted is 2.7 m, then the number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: Using the standard storage capacity formula for a floor area of 54 m² and pile height of 2.7 m, the number of bags works out to approximately 2700.

q: 35. Vicat apparatus is used for
explain: The primary and original use of the Vicat apparatus (with the standard plunger) is to determine the standard consistency of cement paste.

q: 36. Di calcium silicate
options: provides less ultimate strength to cement
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and generates comparatively less heat of hydration than tricalcium silicate, though it contributes to good long-term/ultimate strength.

q: 37. Expansive cement expands mostly during its :
explain: Expansive cement is engineered so that most of its expansion occurs during the final hardening period, after initial set, to compensate for later drying shrinkage.
